title: Third place was a tie

data.workspace: top_sellers.sql, the quarterly top-three bonus list, Marlow Home Furnishings (fictional)

flags.label: Sales director, Grace Owusu
flags.text: Two people in the West region sold exactly 412,000 this quarter, and the bonus list names only one. The rules say anyone tied for a top-three place gets the bonus. Payroll closes at 16:00.

flags.label: Pattern
flags.text: The tied seller left off changes between runs.

flags.label: Payroll
flags.text: 16:00: payroll closed with the bonus list as it stood.

lines.text: WITH r AS (SELECT region, seller, sales,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY sales DESC) AS pos
rank() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY sales DESC) AS pos
dense_rank() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY sales DESC) AS pos
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY sales DESC, seller) AS pos

objective: Rank rows with row_number, rank and dense_rank, and predict how each treats ties
secondaryObjectives: Select the top N rows per group by filtering a ranked subquery or CTE

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. row_number 'Returns the number of the current row within its partition, counting from 1'; rank 'Returns the rank of the current row, with gaps'; dense_rank 'Returns the rank of the current row, without gaps'; rows equal on the ORDER BY columns are peers, and the ranking functions 'give the same answer for all rows of a peer group' (row_number is not one of the four).
Every organization, person, count and deadline is invented teaching data; tool output is an authored rendering in the tool style.

brief.situation: You maintain top_sellers.sql at Marlow Home Furnishings (fictional). It picks the top three sellers per region with row_number() and a filter of 3 or less. In the West, two sellers tied for third; the list names one, and which one changes between runs. The bonus rules say anyone tied for a top-three place qualifies. Payroll closes at 16:00. It is 15:05.
handover: The rules: places are by quarter sales; ties share a place; the next place after a tie is skipped.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

scoring.modelReasoning: A tied seller who appears or disappears between runs points at row_number: it numbers peers in no fixed order. The rules say ties share a place and the next place is skipped, which is exactly rank(). dense_rank does not skip, so Evans would become third; breaking the tie by name is stable but still excludes Diaz. Check each region against the rules.
